Open Evening 2026
Thursday, 24 September 2026 (5-8pm)
Come along with your child to explore our facilities, speak to staff and pupils, and see how learning comes to life at Kennet. This evening will give you a full picture of what we offer, helping you make a confident and informed decision ahead of the admissions deadline in October 2026. Places are limited, so early booking is recommended. Booking closes on 21 September or sooner if we reach our capacity.

Computer Science
Computer Science is essential in our digital age, teaching pupils critical skills in programming, problem-solving, and digital literacy. At Kennet School, we offer a comprehensive curriculum which prepares pupils for future technological challenges.
Curriculum Overview
GCSE Computer Science
A Level Computer Science
Key Stage 3
Pupils are introduced to basic programming, digital systems, and computational thinking. Lessons involve practical projects, coding exercises, and exploring the impact of technology on society.
Key Stage 4
Our GCSE Computer Science course covers programming languages, algorithms, data representation and cybersecurity. Pupils undertake projects which develop their coding skills and understand computer systems and networks.
Key Stage 5
Our A Level Computer Science course includes advanced programming, software development and computational theory. Students work on complex projects, learning about data structures, algorithms, and computer architecture.
Facilities
Our Computer Science Department offers a cutting-edge learning environment, featuring state-of-the-art computer labs, the latest software, online resources and a dedicated coding lab exclusively for our Sixth Form students.
We are proud to foster a growing interest in computer science, with an increasing number of girls joining the subject each year. Our pupils have access to a wide range of co-curricular activities, including the Bebras Challenge, OUCC Challenge, Raspberry Pi Competition and House Hackathon, providing them with opportunities to develop their skills beyond the classroom.
To bridge the gap between academics and industry, we regularly host guest speakers from the tech sector and organise industry-related trips, helping pupils understand real-world applications of computer science. Additionally, we are building a specialised library featuring books from the Oxbridge reading list to support pupils preparing for competitive university interviews.
Our department is committed to inspiring the next generation of computer scientists through innovation, engagement and real-world experience.

Drama
Drama enhances creativity, communication, and confidence. At Kennet School, we offer an engaging Drama programme that inspires pupils to express themselves and explore theatrical arts.
Curriculum Overview
A Level Drama & Theatre Studies
Key Stage 3
Pupils develop foundational acting skills, explore different genres, and participate in improvisation and scripted performances. Lessons focus on teamwork, creativity, and self-expression.
Key Stage 4
Our GCSE Drama course covers acting techniques, playwriting, and performance analysis. Pupils perform in various styles, create original works, and study significant plays and practitioners.
Key Stage 5
The A Level Drama & Theatre Studies course involves advanced acting, directing, and theatre studies. Pupils perform complex pieces, analyse theatrical works, as well as undertake research projects.
Facilities
The Drama Department features a fully equipped theatre, rehearsal spaces and modern lighting and sound systems, providing a professional setting for both performances and practice. Pupils regularly perform at events and shows, as well as teaming up with our Dance and Music Departments to put on amazing sell-out whole-school productions. ​​​​​​

pageCache.pageTitle: Kennet School - Sixth Form Musicians Take Centre Stage at Shaw House
pageCache.text:
Sixth Form Musicians Take Centre Stage at Shaw House
Kennet Sixth Form's talented musicians took to the stage at Shaw House for an evening of live performance.
Kennet Sixth Form's musicians took to the stage at Shaw House for an evening of live performance celebrating the talent, dedication and musical journeys of Year 13 students during their time at Kennet School.
The annual recital brought together pupils, staff and families for a varied programme of music, featuring both ensemble and solo performances.
The evening featured performances from the Year 12 Ensemble and Kennet’s Chamber Choir, alongside a series of solo performances from Year 13 students.
Ahead of each solo performance, Mrs Tylden (Head of Music), introduced the students and reflected on their musical journeys at Kennet, from learning new instruments and developing their voices to performing as part of the school’s many musical groups.
The recital highlighted the breadth of musical talent within the Sixth Form and provided an opportunity to celebrate how far students have progressed during their time at the school.
A wide variety of instruments and styles were represented across the evening, with solo performances including voice, clarinet, bass guitar and classical guitar.
Cookie Policy

pageCache.pageTitle: Kennet School - Gold Class Drama at Kennet School
pageCache.text:
Gold Class Drama at Kennet School
Kennet School is delighted to announce that it has retained its ‘Gold Shakespeare School’ status.
Kennet School is delighted to announce that it has retained its ‘Gold Shakespeare School’ status by the Coram Shakespeare Schools Foundation for yet another year, in recognition of its exceptional and sustained commitment to the Shakespeare Schools programme.
This prestigious award reflects Kennet School’s participation in more than seven consecutive festivals, celebrating the dedication, creativity, and hard work of both students and staff in bringing Shakespeare’s works to life on stage year after year.
The accolade recognises the school’s commitment to providing inspiring opportunities, encouraging community engagement by showcasing the talents of its pupils, and embedding personal development through its extensive creative arts programme. The school has also been commended for keeping creativity high on the agenda and supporting pupils in building crucial, transferable skills for their future.
Mrs Preston, Head of Drama, commented: “Kennet’s Drama Department continues to provide exciting opportunities for pupils. Coram Shakespeare Schools Foundation has engaged and developed the imaginations of our young people for over 15 years now. We always have fun, learn new techniques and make memories participating every year!”
Acting Executive Headteacher, Mr Gayler, added: “We know how outstanding our Drama team and pupils are, so it is really nice when others agree with us! Only the most dedicated Shakespeare Schools qualify for the Gold loyalty tier, so this award speaks for itself on the level of effort the Drama Department pours into their curriculum and co-curricular activities.”
Kennet School is immensely proud of this achievement and looks forward to continuing its partnership with Coram Shakespeare Schools Foundation, inspiring future generations through the power of performance.
Cookie Policy

pageCache.pageTitle: Kennet School - Kennet's Sports Personality of the Year 2026
pageCache.text:
Kennet's Sports Personality of the Year 2026
Kennet's annual Sports Personality of the Year Awards Evening celebrated pupil who have excelled in sport.
Kennet School recently celebrated the outstanding achievements of its young athletes at the annual Sports Personality of the Year Awards Evening, recognising sporting success, dedication, leadership and commitment across the school community.
The event brought together pupils, families, staff and special guests to reflect on another exceptional year of sport at Kennet. Throughout the evening, awards were presented to individuals and teams who have demonstrated excellence both in competition and through their contribution to school sport.
The prestigious Sports Personality of the Year Award was presented to Josh Norton, recognising his remarkable achievements and commitment to sport. Josh is a talented county-level cross-country runner and accomplished steeplechase and distance athlete, who has consistently demonstrated dedication and resilience throughout his sporting career, making him a worthy recipient of the school's highest sporting honour.
A special thank you was also made to Kennet’s Sports Leaders. All 14 students gave more than 15 hours of their time volunteering to support House Sport, clubs and primary events, and all passed their Community Sports Leaders Award with flying colours.
Awards were also presented to outstanding performers in each year group:
The Louise Sugden Award, which recognises determination, resilience and commitment to sport, was awarded to O. Macbeth.
The CAD Cup, awarded to pupils who have made an exceptional contribution to sport and the wider sporting community, was presented to H. Beaumont and B. Rogers.
This year's Teams of the Year were the Under 12 Football Team and Under 14 Football Team, both of whom enjoyed highly successful seasons and represented the school with distinction.
Mr Gayler, Acting Headteacher, said: "The Sports Personality of the Year Awards provide a wonderful opportunity to celebrate the perseverance and achievements of our pupils. Whether competing at the highest level, supporting teammates or demonstrating resilience in the face of challenges, every nominee should be incredibly proud of their accomplishments. Congratulations to all of our award winners and thank you to the staff, coaches, families and Sports Leaders who continue to support our pupils' sporting journeys."
The evening served as a fitting celebration of another successful year for Team Kennet and highlighted the strength, depth and inclusive nature of sport across the school. It was also a powerful reminder of the important role sport plays in supporting both mental health and physical wellbeing. The opportunities available at Kennet are second to none, and we are proud to offer such a rich diversity of opportunities that support both participation and performance, enabling every pupil to find a pathway that suits their interests, ambitions and abilities.

pageCache.pageTitle: Kennet School - Kennet Celebrates British Science Week
pageCache.text:
Kennet Celebrates British Science Week
Kennet School marked British Science Week with a busy programme of lunchtime activities.
Kennet School marked British Science Week with a busy programme of lunchtime activities led by the Science Department.
Throughout the week, pupils explored a range of scientific ideas through creative and engaging practical challenges. Activities included ‘tattooing’ bananas using oxidation, building balloon-powered cars from recycled materials, and creating rainbows through chemical reactions.
Pupils also experimented with circuits powered by potato batteries and discovered how water can be boiled in an origami kettle over a Bunsen burner.
The week gave pupils the opportunity to investigate a variety of scientific principles in an enjoyable and interactive way. Other activities focused on the science of the senses, with pupils taking part in taste tests and sensitivity experiments, as well as learning how to send Morse code through optical fibre.
The activities formed part of a wider celebration of science across the school and encouraged pupils to explore scientific ideas beyond the classroom.
Kennet School would like to thank the Science Department for organising such an inspiring and enjoyable week.
Cookie Policy
Latest News

Art & Design
Art & Design shapes our lives: from what we wear and buy, to what we eat, where we live, and what we enjoy. At Kennet School, we provide an environment which inspires our pupils to create!
Curriculum Overview
GCSE Art, Craft & Design
A Level Art, Craft & Design
You may also be interested in exploring Photography
Key Stage 3
Pupils in Years 7-9 work collaboratively and individually with two and three-dimensional media. They learn to deconstruct images, analyse various artists, cultures, and historical periods, and apply this knowledge to their work, becoming both critics and practitioners.
Key Stage 4
We offer GCSE Art, Craft & Design, a two-year course covering techniques such as drawing, painting, graphics, 3D design, printmaking, digital media, and photography. Pupils explore their interests, develop ideas, and work independently.
Key Stage 5
In our Sixth Form, we offer A Level Art, Craft & Design. This two-year course includes a foundation in fine art, printmaking, 3D design, ceramics, and mixed media. Students build a portfolio, leading to a personal investigation and an externally set assignment.
Facilities
Our Art Department is equipped with cutting-edge technology, featuring six art rooms and two darkrooms. Open daily, including lunchtimes and after school, we provide a dedicated space for creative study, especially for our Sixth Form students.

Education & Early Years
Education and Early Years at Kennet School offers a deep understanding of child development, learning theories, and the essential principles of early years' education, preparing students for further study or employment in this rewarding sector.
Curriculum Overview
T Level Education & Early Years
Key Stage 5
On our T Level Education & Early Years course, students will develop knowledge and understanding of the education and early years sector, including learning about how to support child development, behaviour, equality and diversity, special education needs and disability (SEND) and an occupational specialisms, ‘Early Years Educator’. This course offers a mixture of classroom learning and ‘on-the-job’ experience during an industry placement.
Facilities
Education & Early Years is taught in the new T Level building, which is equipped with specialised classrooms that provide students with the tools and materials needed for hands-on learning. Our specialist teaching staff and resources enable students to gain practical experience in a controlled and supportive environment, and to develop the knowledge and skills required to progress either into the world of work or further their educational journey.

English
English is fundamental to developing communication skills, critical thinking, and cultural understanding. At Kennet School, we offer a comprehensive English curriculum that aims to create curious and confident learners who can articulate their own personal views and interpretations.
Curriculum Overview
GCSE English Language
GCSE English Literature
A Level English Language
A Level English Literature
Key Stage 3
Pupils study a range of literary genres, develop writing skills, and engage in speaking and listening activities. Lessons cover classic and contemporary texts, fostering a love for reading.
Key Stage 4
GCSE English Language and GCSE English Literature are mandatory subjects at Kennet. Pupils analyse literary texts, develop advanced writing skills, and practise critical reading. The course includes novels, poetry, plays and non-fiction.
Key Stage 5
Our A Level English Language course explores language use, linguistics and discourse analysis. The A Level English Literature course involves in-depth study of literary texts, critical theory and thematic analysis. Both courses prepare students for higher education and careers requiring strong analytical and communication skills.
Facilities
Our teaching staff have a passion for literature, a wealth of experience and a well-stocked book cupboard. Throughout the year, pupils are encouraged to participate in poetry, creative writing, public speaking, debating and mock trial competitions. We also organise regular theatre trips, not only to deepen pupils' understanding of studied texts but also to foster a love of literature and cultural experiences.

pageCache.pageTitle: Kennet School - Kennet Celebrates Third Platinum Artsmark Award
pageCache.text:
Kennet Celebrates Third Platinum Artsmark Award
The award recognises Kennet's long-standing commitment to high-quality arts education.
Kennet School is celebrating after being awarded the Artsmark Platinum Award for the third consecutive time, recognising its exceptional commitment to arts education and creativity across the whole school.
The Platinum Award is the highest accolade presented by Artsmark and celebrates schools that place the arts at the heart of their curriculum and wider school community. Receiving the award for a third time reflects Kennet's sustained commitment to ensuring every pupil has access to high-quality creative opportunities. As the Artsmark Award is renewed every two years, Kennet School has now held Platinum status for six consecutive years.
In their assessment, Artsmark praised Kennet School's ‘deeply embedded and highly mature arts culture’, highlighting the school's commitment to maintaining dedicated curriculum time for Art, Music, Dance and Drama, alongside an extensive range of GCSE, A Level and vocational pathways.
Assessors also recognised the school's innovative Arts Open Month, which brings together teachers from primary and secondary schools to share best practice through workshops, lesson observations, performances, professional dialogue and film production. They commended Kennet's strong partnerships with organisations including the Royal Opera House, Watermill Theatre, Berkshire Music Trust and the University of Reading, as well as its commitment to ensuring the arts are accessible to all pupils through inclusive provision and enrichment opportunities.
The report also celebrated the leadership opportunities available to pupils, noting how they take responsibility for directing productions, choreography, stage management and technical roles, whilst developing valuable skills that extend beyond the classroom.
Mr M Gayler, Acting Headteacher, said: "We are incredibly proud to have achieved the Platinum Artsmark Award for the third consecutive time. This reflects the passion, expertise and dedication of our staff, the enthusiasm and creativity of our pupils, and the value we place on providing an education that develops the whole child.
"The arts play a vital role in inspiring confidence and helping pupils discover and develop their talents. We remain committed to ensuring creativity continues to thrive at Kennet, both through our curriculum and the wealth of opportunities available beyond the classroom.
"I would like to thank everyone who has contributed to this achievement, particularly our Art, Drama, Dance and Music departments, whose commitment continue to provide exceptional experiences for our pupils."
The Artsmark assessors concluded that Kennet School has established an arts-rich culture that not only benefits its own pupils but also supports the wider education sector by sharing expertise and championing creative practice.
Cookie Policy
Latest News

pageCache.pageTitle: Kennet School - National Recognition for Reflection & Leadership
pageCache.text:
National Recognition for Reflection & Leadership
Kennet receives national accreditation by SSAT for its work in developing a culture of reflection and leadership driven by moral purpose.
Kennet School has been awarded national accreditation by SSAT in recognising its work in developing a culture of reflection and leadership driven by moral purpose.
The accreditation, part of SSAT’s Framework of Exceptional Education, recognises the school’s work in these areas as among the most effective practice nationally.
The recognition highlights Kennet’s long-standing commitment to reflective leadership, where leaders at all levels are encouraged to review and refine their work to ensure decisions are consistently guided by what is right for pupils.
Central to the accreditation is the school’s focus on leadership with moral purpose, ensuring that values, integrity and the best interests of pupils remain at the heart of decision-making across the school.
Mr A Tucker, Kennet School’s Assistant Headteacher and SSAT Lead, said: "This accreditation reflects something that is deeply embedded in our culture. Reflection is not a one-off exercise at Kennet but an ongoing commitment to improving what we do for our pupils.
"It is very much a collective achievement and a credit to colleagues across the school who are dedicated to leading with moral purpose and principle."
The accreditation process involved external evaluation against national standards, exploring how leadership and values translate into meaningful impact across the school community. This recognition further strengthens Kennet School’s reputation for high-quality education and principled leadership.
Cookie Policy
Latest News

pageCache.pageTitle: Kennet School - Kennet Games Returns for a Day of Inclusive Sport
pageCache.text:
Kennet Games Returns for a Day of Inclusive Sport
Pupils from across the local area came together for a day of inclusive sport, teamwork and shared experiences.
On Saturday 2 May, Kennet School hosted it’s 48th Kennet Games - a much-loved event that brings together children with disabilities from across the local area for a day of sport, activity and shared experiences.
A long-standing part of the school calendar, Kennet Games once again showed the importance of inclusive sport. A range of activities were on offer, including table cricket, basketball shoot, javelin, skittles, rollaball, quadra throw, velcro target, table skittles, precision bean bag, shuffleboard, boccia and a series of races, giving every participant the chance to take part.
We were pleased to welcome pupils from Charters School, Lambs Lane School, Speenhamland School and PALS. Their enthusiasm set the tone for the day, with support and encouragement at every turn.
Events like this rely on a huge team effort, and the Games were made possible thanks to the dedication of staff, volunteers and supporters who helped everything run so smoothly. Thank you also to Kennet School PTAC for providing refreshments, and to Swings & Smiles for setting up a sensory station.
Acting Headteacher, Mr M Gayler, said: "This event is an important part of what we do as a school. It’s about creating opportunities for every young person to take part, feel included and enjoy being active. The atmosphere on the day said everything: supportive, encouraging and full of pure joy. Thank you to everyone who helped make it happen, and to all the participants who made the day so memorable."
Kennet Games continue to bring people together through sport, with this year’s event once again showing just how powerful those opportunities can be.
Cookie Policy
Latest News

pageCache.pageTitle: Kennet School - Months of Dedication Bring Billy Elliot to Life
pageCache.text:
Months of Dedication Bring Billy Elliot to Life
Kennet School's annual summer musical brought together pupils from across the school to stage an ambitious production of Billy Elliot.
Kennet School's talented pupils wowed audiences with three outstanding performances of this year's summer musical, Billy Elliot, bringing months of commitment and creativity to the stage.
From the opening scene to the final curtain call, pupils impressed audiences with their acting, singing, dancing and musicianship, whilst the backstage crew ensured every performance ran seamlessly. The production demonstrated not only exceptional talent, but also the teamwork and resilience developed through months of rehearsals alongside pupils' academic studies. It reflected the school's values of resilience, courage and commitment, whilst highlighting how opportunities beyond the classroom form an integral part of Kennet's broad and ambitious co-curricular offer and education in its broadest sense.
The success of the production was made possible through the dedication of Kennet's Drama, Dance and Music departments, together with the wider production team. Countless hours were spent planning rehearsals, choreography, music, costumes, lighting, sound and stage management to bring the much-loved musical to life.
Mr M Gayler, Acting Headteacher, said: "Every member of the cast, band and backstage crew should be incredibly proud of what they achieved. I thoroughly enjoyed watching the show, and it was clear from the moment it began just how much hard work had gone into every aspect of the production. Productions of this scale demand an enormous amount of commitment, and it was fantastic to see our pupils performing with such confidence and professionalism.
"I would like to thank our Drama, Dance and Music departments, the wider production team and everyone who worked tirelessly behind the scenes to make the performances possible. Their dedication gave our pupils the opportunity to create something special, with memories they’ll never forget.”
The school would like to congratulate every pupil who took part, both on stage and behind the scenes, for their contribution to another fantastic summer production. Kennet School also extends its thanks to the many families, friends and members of the local community who filled the auditorium across the three performances and supported the cast with such enthusiasm.
The annual summer musical is a highlight of the school calendar, providing pupils with the opportunity to develop their confidence and creativity whilst sharing their talents with the wider community.
Cookie Policy

Business Studies
Business Studies equips pupils with practical knowledge and skills about the dynamic world of commerce and entrepreneurship. At Kennet School, we provide a stimulating environment which fosters critical thinking and business acumen.
Curriculum Overview
GCSE Business Studies
A Level Business Studies
T Level Management & Administration
You may also be interested in also exploring Economics.
Key Stage 4
Our GCSE Business course covers fundamental concepts such as marketing, finance, operations, and human resources. Pupils learn about business ethics, entrepreneurship, and the economic environment, developing skills through case studies and real-world applications.
Key Stage 5
We offer two business-related courses in the Sixth Form: A Level Business Studies and T Level Business Management & Administration. Both courses are two-years' duration.
The A Level Business course delves deeper into business strategy, decision-making, and global business issues. Pupils analyse complex business scenarios, conduct market research, and explore business operations in various contexts.
The T Level Business Management & Administration course offers a minimum of nine weeks' hands-on practical experience working with an employer on an industry placement. Pupils will develop an understanding of a broad range of issues relevant to the sector, including business context, project and change management, business behaviours, quality and compliance, plus two specialisms (business administration and business support).
Facilities
The Business Department features modern classrooms with interactive technology and access to business simulation software, providing pupils with hands-on experience in managing and analysing business operations. Throughout the academic year, we host a wide range of co-curricular opportunities for pupils, including trips and guest speakers, as well as work placement opportunities which offer hands-on experience in their chosen fields.

Child Development
Child Development at Kennet School equips pupils with the knowledge and practical skills needed for careers in childcare and education. Our engaging curriculum fosters an understanding of child growth, development and the essentials of early years' education.
Curriculum Overview
Level 2 Child Development
Key Stage 4
Our Level 2 Child Development course is a vocational course, which means it is more practical-based and assessed predominantly via coursework. It is a two-year course which gives pupils the skills and confidence to work with young children. Pupils not only gain academic knowledge but also gain practical skills needed to work within the childcare industry - from nutritional and well-being needs to understanding the developmental norms of a child from birth to five years of age.
Following on from this course, pupils usually select either of our Sixth Form T Level courses: Education & Early Years or Health.
Facilities
Kennet School offers excellent facilities to support Child Development classes, providing pupils with a practical and engaging learning environment. Our classrooms are equipped with a range of learning materials to simulate real early years settings and help pupils develop hands-on experience in childcare and education.

Construction
Construction at Kennet School provides pupils with practical skills and knowledge for a career in the construction industry. We offer a hands-on learning environment which prepares pupils for future vocational opportunities.
Curriculum Overview
Level 2 Construction
Key Stage 4
Our Level 2 Construction course is a vocational course, which means it is more practical-based and assessed predominantly via coursework. The course content is designed to give pupils a comprehensive introduction to the construction industry. Pupils learn essential skills in areas such as carpentry, bricklaying, painting and decorating and tiling. The course also covers health and safety, construction technology and project management.
Throughout the course, pupils undertake practical projects which simulate real-world construction tasks. They develop technical skills, problem-solving abilities and an understanding of the construction process from planning to completion. The curriculum is tailored to provide a strong foundation for those looking to pursue further education or apprenticeships in construction.
Facilities
Construction is an integral part of Kennet’s Design & Technology Department, offering a dedicated bricklaying compound and fully equipped facilities for hands-on learning. Pupils have access to the tools and materials needed to develop practical skills in carpentry, tiling, painting and decorating. This supportive environment ensures they gain real-world experience while building confidence and expertise.
We are committed to providing an enriching and dynamic environment that nurtures creativity, confidence and real-world skills for our future tradesmen!

Dance
Dance fosters physical fitness, creativity, and expressive skills. At Kennet School, we offer a vibrant Dance programme which nurtures talent and encourages artistic growth.
Curriculum Overview
* Dance is taught on rotation in Key Stage 3 as part of Physical Edication (PE).
Key Stage 3
While studying Dance at Key Stage 3, pupils explore a range of styles and professional works. Lessons focus on building physical technique, developing creative choreography, enhancing performance skills and fostering the ability to evaluate both peer and self-performances.
Key Stage 4
Our two-year GCSE Dance course provides a solid foundation for pupils looking to pursue further studies in dance and performing arts. Pupils will perform both a solo and a duet/trio in a contemporary style, then choreograph their own piece in a style of their choice, ensuring it aligns with the stimulus set by the exam board. They will also explore a diverse anthology of professional works, enhancing their ability to critically analyse different dance styles and cultural influences.
Key Stage 5
The A Level Dance course equips students with the skills and experience needed for success both in the performing arts industry and beyond. Through live performances, mastering high-quality dance techniques, and creating innovative choreography inspired by external stimuli, students refine their craft and showcase their abilities in assessed performances. Additionally, they develop critical thinking skills by analysing professional works, exploring historical events, and understanding the social contexts that have shaped our world.
Facilities
The Dance Department utilises our versatile Hall space equipped with sound systems, as well as the Kennet Leisure Dance Studio and a dedicated ballet barre studio with free-standing barres and mirrors - all creating the perfect setting for practice and performance. Pupils frequently showcase their talents at events and shows, as well as collaborating with the Drama and Music Departments to deliver spectacular, sell-out whole school productions. ​​​​​​
